description: the discriminating twin of when-firing-counts-against-budget at the SAME instruction budget of 2: that handler's body is empty and IS delivered, this one's body holds a statement and is REFUSED. A handler must afford its firing AND, when its body has statements, its body's first statement - executeStatements runs that first statement only while the count is below the budget on entry, so a non-empty handler admitted at the boundary would emit its block-head and then halt having run nothing. The proof is an ABSENCE that a source-to-events fold observes directly: there is exactly one ProfileStatement instruction event here, the when registration itself, and no second one for a handler start. Dropping the body-gate arm admits the handler and adds that orphan block-head event
